title: SIBM in the crawler class, re-issued with runs long enough: from a random field, layered wave-pinning cells form and the surviving crawler moves 4.2, 3.2 and 3.6 of its own diameters merger-free by t=32 on seeds 0-2, with its self-made layer on every body-frame; the linear-kinetics twin never moves
summary: world.py is c31's crawlers-from-noise world (20261026T0406-c31-crawlers-from-noise-claim, unchanged), whose SIBM claim is disputed on M because at its t=16 the crawlers had moved only 1.4-3.6 labkit body lengths (my review 20261026T1001-c39-review-crawlers-noise: 2.1-2.3 own diameters at t=16, 4.8 at t=32 on seed 17). Same world, labkit seeds 0-2, 160 frames (t=32). From a smoothed random two-phase field, curvature flow leaves 6-9 round cells by t~1.5, each with a ring of its own layer species s (made by the bound polarity protein); the larger ones polarize into half-moon crawlers that absorb the static cells they touch, and one large crawler remains (components final 1 on all seeds, occupancy 0.22-0.29). Measured on the unwrapped labkit track in units of the body's own diameter (crawlpath.py), the crawler travels 4.20 (seed 0, track 35, t=8.6-32), 3.22 (seed 1, track 32, t=1.2-15, ends by merging) and 3.63 (seed 2, track 31, t=10.4-32) diameters with path = net (straight). The s layer passes a signed-distance test on 100% of body-frames from t=8 (rim |d| <= 3 px vs core d <= -10 and outside 6-15 px: median rim/core 3.5-3.8, rim/out 19-21). Controls on seed 0: KIN=1 linear polarity kinetics, no cell moves (0.03 diameters to t=32); SRC=none, the layer vanishes (flat s, 0% of body-frames) while the same crawler moves as before.

claims.statement: From a random two-phase field (seeds 0, 1, 2; t=32), round cells form, each with a ring of a layer species its own polarity protein makes; the surviving crawler of each run keeps that ring on every body-frame and crawls 3.2-4.2 of its own diameters along a straight path without merging, with its half-moon shape kept.
claims.track: seed 0, track 35 (pack/seed0/sheet.png t=8.6-32, pack/seed0/tracks.png): a layered half-moon crawler of diameter ~2.7 units that travels 4.20 own diameters merger-free from t=8.6 to t=32, layer rim/core 3.5, rim/out 19

controls_run.M: linear/seed0 (KIN=1 linear polarity kinetics, t=32): no movement (0.03 diameters)
controls_run.B: nosrc/seed0 (SRC=none): s flat, 0% of body-frames pass, cells unchanged

claims.bd_control: linear/seed0 (KIN=1: the bistable polarity kinetics replaced by linear relaxation): no polarization, no motion

limitations: The population coarsens to a single large crawler (diameter ~55% of the box) by absorbing static cells, so the motile individual is a merger product and I at late times is one body; merger-free runs are measured from the last merge. Seed 1's run ends in a merge at t=15 (3.22 diameters). The layer's adsorption flux is written against the body field (Langmuir flux up grad 4phi(1-phi)); it counts through the self-made-source clause, and the layer does no work for motion (s acts back on nothing). rho starts near its high state (1 +- 0.2) as in c31's claim. No division.
